stem: (Select TWO.) Pemberton Robotics' child module has a `locals` block, and a teammate wants to reuse one of those local values directly from the parent module. Which two statements about how locals, variables, and outputs actually behave are correct?

choices.text: A value defined in a `locals` block is accessible only in the module that defines it
A parent module can read a child module's local values directly with `module.<NAME>.<LOCAL_NAME>` syntax
A `locals` block accepts a value from outside the module at run time, the same way a `variable` block does
A `locals` block always mirrors the value of an `output` block with the matching name in the same module
A `locals` block is referenced elsewhere in the module with `local.<NAME>`, the singular form of the block's own plural name `locals`

rationale: c is wrong; a parent module can only reach a child's output blocks, never its locals directly. d is wrong; a locals block computes its value from an expression inside the module, it does not accept an externally supplied value the way a variable does. e is wrong; there is no automatic mirroring between a local and an output of the same name -- an output only exposes what its own value argument computes.
